title: Result
description: One upper or lower bound for one problem in one model. Results that follow from other results via reductions are not stored; they are derived on demand.

title.description: Short descriptive name, e.g. 'Maximal matching via rounding'.

reduce_to.description: Id of the result this one is obtained from by a reduction (see data/reductions/), e.g. a maximal matching algorithm from an MIS algorithm on the line graph. Left out for algorithms that solve the problem directly.

decomposition.description: Output parameters, for network decomposition: number of cluster colors, cluster diameter, and whether the diameter is weak (measured in G) or strong (inside the cluster).

colors.description: Number of colors, for coloring problems. Same format as runtime.

variant.description: For degree splitting: 'directed' (orient the edges so that in- and out-degree are balanced) or 'undirected' (color the edges red and blue so that both colors are balanced).

discrepancy.description: Maximum discrepancy at a node, for degree splitting: the difference between in- and out-degree (directed) or between red and blue degree (undirected). Same format as runtime.

via.description: Id of the reduction used to obtain this result from reduce_to, when several reductions connect the same two problems (e.g. two kinds of shattering).

graph_class.description: Most general graph class the result holds for.

assumptions.description: Extra input or knowledge the algorithm relies on.

year.description: Year of the earliest publication of the result (including preprints).

url.description: Link to the referenced theorem, e.g. in the HTML version on arXiv (see scripts/link_theorems.py).

comments.description: Short note, not a full sentence, e.g. 'reduction to MIS'. [[result-id]] links a result, e.g. 'Theorem 15 applied to [[mm-pr01-forest-decomposition]]'; [[paper-id]] links a paper.

latex.description: Display form, as written in the paper.

expr.description: Machine-readable form. Variables: n, Delta, D (the diameter; runtimes with D are not compared). Functions: log, logstar, sqrt, poly, O, Otilde, Omega, Theta, and min with several arguments. Constants: eps, delta, gamma, lambda (fixed constants of a result; lambda is the arboricity, for bounded-arboricity graphs). Operators: + - * / ^ and parentheses. Example: 'O(log(Delta)^2 * log(n))'.
